Routine Descriptions

SRSCAN_ASI_MAP_SET

 [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_asi_map_set

PURPOSE:
  Prepare a map canvas for srs_canada all-sky imager mosaics.

  Unlike the THEMIS thm_map_set (8-bit color-table graphics), this canvas
  runs in DECOMPOSED 24-bit color throughout, which is what lets truecolor
  (RGB) imager data render with real colors: continents, background, grid
  and annotations are 24-bit long values ('BBGGRR'x), and the mosaic
  drivers polyfill with R + 256L*G + 65536L*B.

  Defaults center on the TREx array (computed from srscan_trex_rgb_sites).

KEYWORDS:
  scale:            map_set scale (default 14e6)
  central_lat:      geographic latitude of plot center (default: TREx centroid)
  central_lon:      geographic longitude of plot center (default: TREx centroid)
  color_continent:  24-bit fill color for land (default dark gray)
  color_background: 24-bit background color (default near-black)
  position:         plot position in normal coordinates
  xsize, ysize:     window/buffer size in pixels (default 800x600)
  noerase:          do not erase the current window
  zbuffer:          render into the Z buffer (headless-safe)
  projection:       map_set projection name (default 'mercator')
  window:           direct-graphics window number
  rotation:         map rotation (degrees)

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/mosaic/srscan_asi_map_set.pro)

SRSCAN_TREX_RGB_GRID_PLOT

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_trex_rgb_grid_plot

PURPOSE:
  Render one frame of a loaded MOSv001 grid variable
  (srscan_trexrgb_grid) onto the srs_canada map canvas in truecolor.

  The MOSv001 grids are the OFFICIAL archive mosaic rendering, so this
  is the ground truth to compare srscan_trex_rgb_mosaic output against
  (geometry and color).

  The grid cells are regular in lon/lat, so each frame is warped to the
  map projection with map_patch per channel and displayed with tv,/true;
  fill cells (-999) stay transparent (map background shows through).

INPUT:
  time: time of the frame to render (string or double); the nearest
        loaded frame is used

KEYWORDS:
  varname:  tplot variable to render (default 'srscan_trexrgb_grid')
  minval, maxval: linear intensity stretch (same window for R,G,B;
        default minval=0, maxval=255 -- the DN are already display-ish)
  png_out:  write the canvas to this PNG file
  mosaic_image: (out) rendered [3,xs,ys] image
  no_label: skip annotation
  and the srscan_asi_map_set canvas keywords:
  scale, central_lat, central_lon, projection, rotation, position,
  xsize, ysize, noerase, window, zbuffer, color_continent, color_background

EXAMPLE:
  srscan_load_trex_rgb, datatype='grid', time='2023-03-24/06:22:30'
  srscan_trex_rgb_grid_plot, '2023-03-24/06:22:30', /zbuffer, png_out='grid.png'

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/mosaic/srscan_trex_rgb_grid_plot.pro)

SRSCAN_TREX_RGB_MOSAIC

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_trex_rgb_mosaic

PURPOSE:
  Render a TRUECOLOR mosaic of the TREx RGB all-sky imager array at a
  given time: each camera's frame is projected onto a geographic map
  through its skymap (110 km), painted pixel-by-pixel with 24-bit
  decomposed color so the RGB data keep their real colors.

INPUT:
  time: 'YYYY-MM-DD/hh:mm:ss' (19 characters)

KEYWORDS (selection):
  sites:    site uid(s) to include (default: all from srscan_trex_rgb_sites)
  exclude:  site uid(s) to skip
  minimum_elevation: don't paint pixels below this elevation (default 8 deg)

KEYWORDS (intensity scaling; same window applied to R,G,B to preserve
color balance):
  minval, maxval: linear stretch window (DN); scalars. Default: per-site
                  auto stretch anchored at the median illuminated luma.

KEYWORDS (map/canvas, passed to srscan_asi_map_set):
  scale, central_lat, central_lon, projection, rotation, position,
  xsize, ysize, noerase, window, zbuffer,
  color_continent, color_background

KEYWORDS (multi-frame):
  stoptime:  'YYYY-MM-DD/hh:mm:ss'; render frames from time to stoptime
  timestep:  seconds between frames (default 3)

KEYWORDS (output/annotation):
  png_out:  string filename -> write a PNG; with stoptime, one PNG per
            frame named MOSA.<timestamp>.png in png_dir
  png_dir:  output directory for the stoptime PNG series (default '.')
  mosaic_image: (out) the rendered [3, xsize, ysize] truecolor image
  no_grid:  skip the geographic grid overlay
  no_label: skip the timestamp/network annotation
  no_download, verbose: passthrough

EXAMPLES:
  srscan_trex_rgb_mosaic, '2023-03-24/06:22:30'
  srscan_trex_rgb_mosaic, '2023-03-24/06:22:30', /zbuffer, $
    png_out='mosaic.png', minval=15, maxval=120

NOTES:
  Pixels are painted in order of increasing elevation per site, so where
  fields of view overlap the higher-elevation (better) view wins.

SRSCAN_TREX_RGB_MOSAIC_ARRAY

 [Previous Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_trex_rgb_mosaic_array

PURPOSE:
  Build the per-site pixel arrays a TREx RGB mosaic is rendered from:
  for every requested site, load the frame nearest the requested time,
  fetch the site's skymap, and emit flattened per-pixel image values,
  geographic corner polygons, elevations, and an illuminated flag.

  Skymaps are consumed NATIVELY (full_map_latitude/longitude corner grids
  at 110 km, full_elevation) -- no THEMIS-style calibration adapter.
  All arrays get the one srscan_trex_rgb_orient transform so images and
  geometry stay aligned.

INPUT:
  time:   'YYYY-MM-DD/hh:mm:ss' (or unix double) -- frame nearest this
          time (+-1.5 s) is used per site
  sites:  string array of site uids to include

OUTPUT (positional):
  img1:   fltarr[n1, 3, n_sites]  dark-subtracted RGB pixel values
  cor1:   fltarr[n1, 4, 2, n_sites]  corner (lon,lat) polygons at 110 km
  ele1:   fltarr[n1, n_sites]  pixel elevation angles (deg)
  www1:   intarr[n1, n_sites]  1 = pixel imaged and corners finite, -1 = not
  n_sites: number of sites in the arrays (= n_elements(sites))
  (n1 = 553*480; rows are sorted by increasing elevation per site so the
   driver paints low-elevation pixels first and overlaps favor the
   higher-elevation view)

KEYWORDS:
  exclude:     site uid(s) to skip
  no_download: offline mode passthrough
  verbose:     dprint verbosity

NOTES:
  Corner extraction uses ALL-ARRAY subscripts: in IDL,
  arr[scalar, ivec, jvec] is a CROSS PRODUCT of the subscript vectors;
  element-wise pairing requires every subscript to be an array, which is
  why the corner lookups below are done with full index arrays into the
  flattened [554,481] grids.

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/mosaic/srscan_trex_rgb_mosaic_array.pro)
